voyage.name: Berlin Tour by public bus line 100 and 200
voyage.content: The 100 and 200 bus lines are just ordinary bus lines, but they pass by many of Berlin's famous landmarks. Both run every 5–10 minutes between S+U-station Zoologischer Garten and S+U-station Alexanderplatz. All BVG tickets are accepted.

voyage.name: Stern und Kreisschiffahrt
voyage.content: By far the biggest boat company in Berlin. They offer tours on most lakes.

voyage.name: Segway Tour Berlin
voyage.content: Offers different Segway Sightseeing Tours in Berlin. Start near Brandenburger Tor, for small groups up to 10 people.

voyage.name: Ticket B
voyage.content: Showing the city of Berlin on hand-picked architectural routes. Led by architects in German, English, French, Italian or Spanish. Tours from the water, on land or in a helicopter are offered. They arrange your special tour on contemporary architecture in Berlin with many exclusive visits to the interiors of buildings.

voyage.name: Yachtcharter Werder
voyage.content: Offers the possibility of a long-term stay on the waterways of Berlin and the surrounding federal state Brandenburg.

voyage.name: Ultraschall Berlin - Festival für neue Musik
voyage.content: An annual festival begun in 1999 that is dedicated to new music featuring both world premieres and music by recent composers. Concerts take place in different venues across the city and are performed by small ensembles up to big orchestras.

voyage.name: Berlinale – Berlin Film Festival
voyage.content: The city's largest cultural event and an important fixture in the global film industry's calendar (up there with Cannes). 250,000 tickets sold, 400 different films screened and a host of associated parties and events every year. In contrast to Cannes, all screenings at the Berlinale are open to the public. Tickets are inexpensive and relatively easy to get for the "International Forum of Young Film" screenings and th

voyage.name: MaerzMusik
voyage.content: A festival with contemporary music and performances on issues of our time, organised by Berliner Festspiele.

voyage.name: Fête de la Musique
voyage.content: All kinds of music around the city on this day coordinating with a similar day in most French cities.

voyage.name: Young Euro Classic
voyage.content: A music festival established in 2000 that features youth orchestras from around the world. The concerts take place in the Konzerthaus Berlin on Gendarmenmarkt. The festival usually runs for around 2 weeks. Concerts often feature world premieres.

voyage.name: Lange Nacht der Museen
voyage.price: Adults €23, concessions €17, under 12 free. Ticket includes unlimited use of the shuttle bus service and public transportation (BVG and S-Bahn). If you buy in advance the tickets are cheaper
voyage.content: A large cultural event with many museums (around 80) open until 02:00 and extra events around the city.

voyage.name: Doors Open Day of the Federal Government
voyage.alt: Tag der offenen Tür der Bundesregierung
voyage.content: For one weekend, the federal government organises doors open days where most of the Federal Ministries and other governmental institutions can be accessed. Parts of the German Chancellery are also accessible, where the current chancellor will usually show up. Free transport between the locations is provided. There are security checks and they advise to avoid bringing larger objects (such as suitcases). Bring an offic

voyage.name: Musikfest Berlin
voyage.content: A large classical music festival marking the beginning of the season. For about 2 weeks there are concerts in many of Berlin's music venues. Renowned international and German orchestras perform. Organised by Berliner Festspiele.

voyage.name: Festival of Lights
voyage.content: A 10-day-long festival when famous buildings in Berlin are illuminated in a special way.

voyage.name: Karneval
voyage.hours: In late February or early March
voyage.content: As a lot of people came to Berlin from the southern or western area of Germany where Fasching, Fastnacht or Karneval is celebrated, a carnival parade was also established in Berlin. It grew bigger and bigger (about 500,000 to 1 million people watching), but the costumes and cars are rather boring and the people are not as dressed up as in the "original" big carnival parades (Cologne, Mainz, Düsseldorf). Since 2007 th

voyage.name: Karneval der Kulturen
voyage.hours: In May or June (on Whit Sun)
voyage.content: The idea of the "Carnival of Cultures" is a parade of the various ethnic groups of the city showing traditional music, costumes and dances. Other more modern, alternative and political groups also participate. Similar events are also held in Hamburg and Frankfurt.

voyage.name: Christopher Street Day
voyage.content: Berlin's Pride is one of the largest and most vibrant LGBTQIA+ events in the world. While it remains a serious political demonstration for equal rights and protection against discrimination, it is equally famous for its massive, carnival-like atmosphere. Even for those not involved in the movement, the parade is a spectacular sight, featuring elaborate floats, wild costumes, and techno beats that turn the city center

voyage.name: Fuckparade
voyage.content: It was founded in 1997 as a counter-movement to the commercialized Love Parade, and has evolved into an annual political demonstration for the preservation of Berlin's underground club culture and against gentrification. Unlike mainstream techno events, this parade focuses on extreme electronic music such as Gabber, Hardcore, and Breakcore. It remains strictly non-commercial, featuring political speeches and a convoy

voyage.name: Hanf Parade
voyage.content: The Hanfparade is Europe's largest political demonstration for the legalization and normalization of cannabis. Even after Germany's partial legalization in 2024, it remains a massive annual event focused on further reforms and full commercial integration. While the atmosphere regarding consumption has become much more relaxed, visitors should stay mindful of public consumption rules (especially staying away from mino

voyage.name: Basketball
voyage.content: Alba Berlin, known as The Albatross are consistently among the best basketball teams in Germany, and one of the best in Europe. Their erstwhile dominance of the German league has been challenged by the upstart Bayern Munich basketball division flush with cash from the soccer division of the same club. Expect a fierce atmosphere and a packed hall for games against Munich or their traditional rival Bamberg. With fans c

voyage.name: Public swimming pools
voyage.content: Can be found around the city. Check out BBB for pool listings and opening times.

voyage.name: Ice hockey
voyage.content: The Berlin Eisbären (Polar Bears) play this fast, exciting and very physical sport during the winter. The excitement is heightened by the singing and chanting of the crowds, who are fueled by the copious quantities of wurst and beer available.

voyage.name: Australian Football
voyage.content: The Berlin Crocodiles host regular matches in the summer.

voyage.name: Spandau Citadel
voyage.content: A fortress built between 1560 and 1590 to Italian design on the site of a 12th-century castle. The Juliusturm housed part of the huge indemnity (in physical gold coins) France had to pay after the war of 1870/71 until what was left of it was returned to France after Germany's loss in World War I. The term "Juliusturm" remained in usage in German for a large "rainy day fund" into the 1960s. Museums housed within the c

voyage.name: St. Nikolai Church
voyage.content: A splendid 15th-century Gothic church with many fine accoutrements.

voyage.name: Militärhistorisches Museum der Bundeswehr – Flugplatz Berlin-Gatow
voyage.content: At a former Luftwaffe and Royal Air Force (RAF) airfield, RAF Gatow. The museum's focus is on military history, particularly the history of the Luftwaffe of the Bundeswehr, with a collection of more than 200,000 items, including 155 aeroplanes, 5,000 uniforms and 30,000 books. There are also displays (including aeroplanes) on the history of the airfield when it was used by the RAF. Aircraft include reproductions of O

voyage.name: Schloss Tegel
voyage.hours: Guided tours Mondays from May to Sept
voyage.content: A remarkable medium-sized classical castle by the famous K.F. Schinkel built 1820 to 1824, also called "Humboldtschlösschen", because Alexander and Wilhelm von Humboldt (and their family) lived here once. Still privately owned.

voyage.name: Dicke Marie
voyage.content: Not far away from Schloss Tegel (at the "große Malche") you can take a look at the oldest tree in Berlin, an oak which has been growing there since about 1192 (so it's actually older than Berlin itself). The name ("fat Mary") allegedly stems from the brother Humboldt who named the tree after their overweight cook.

voyage.name: IBA-Bauten at Tegeler Hafen
voyage.content: During the International Building Exhibition 1984 to 1988 a bunch of remarkable buildings were set around the old Tegeler Hafen. Architecturally diverse, the most important is the Phosphateliminierungsanlage (Gustav Peichl). Also some buildings by Charles Moore are interesting.

voyage.name: Borsigwerke and Borsigturm
voyage.content: Ex-industrial buildings from the late 19th and early 20th century, nice clinker-architecture and the first (mini) highraiser of Berlin, the Borsigturm, 65 m high, built 1922-24. The area houses now offices, a shopping mall and some places for entertainment. The company Borsig has a very turbulent and storied history and while it has long since ceased being a "German" company or connected to the family of the same nam

voyage.name: Alt Lübars
voyage.content: One of the most authentic and oldest villages (1247) in the outskirts of Berlin, it looks the same way it did some hundred years ago. Take S-Bahn 1 to Waidmannslust and then bus 222 to Alt-Lübars.

voyage.name: Greenwich Promenade
voyage.content: Relaxing lake-side strolls on 'Greenwich Promenaid', a path named after Reinickendorf's twin town of Greenwich, London.

voyage.name: Sommerbad Staaken-West
voyage.content: An outdoor 25-m pool.

voyage.name: Stadtbad Spandau Nord
voyage.content: An indoor pool built 1911 in the neo-baroque style.

voyage.name: Kombibad Spandau Süd
voyage.content: 50-m pool

voyage.name: Strandbad Lübars
voyage.content: A well-equipped beach

voyage.name: Paracelsus Bad
voyage.content: 25 m pool

voyage.name: Borsighallen
voyage.content: A nice shopping mall located in Tegel. It's converted locomotive assembly halls turned into a typical medium sized Berlin mall with every shop you'll need. Additionally there is a cinema and other entertainment stuff.

voyage.name: Markthalle Tegel
voyage.content: Indoor food market. Fantastic fresh foods at local prices, including bakers, deli counters, and greengrocers.

voyage.name: Märkisches Zentrum
voyage.content: The main mall in Märkisches Viertel

voyage.name: Restaurant Aarju
voyage.content: Indian-Singaporean food busy on weekends, reservation recommended

voyage.name: Fishermans Restaurant
voyage.content: A fish place with a terrace with views of the lake

voyage.name: Casa Schmuck
voyage.content: Maybe the sweetest little bed and breakfast place in Berlin. Outside the center in Spandau, close to lakes and rivers, to the Olympic Stadium and the convention center. The lady running it is really nice!

voyage.name: Hostel Berlin Altstadt Spandau
voyage.content: 5 minutes away from U Altstadt Spandau.

voyage.name: Hettler & Lange Hotel und City-Camping
voyage.content: A nice campsite and small hotel next to the river. The amenities are quite basic, but clean and sufficient. Not suitable for people who need absolute silence for a good sleep - but the noise from the nearby Tegel airport is not very hard to get used to.

voyage.name: Tierpark
voyage.content: The zoo in the former East Berlin is more spacious than its West Berlin counterpart, the historic Berlin Zoo and has been open for some 50 years. The Tierpark has nearly as many animals, but fewer reptiles and aquatic animals. It appears rather like a park with animals than a classic zoo, in fact it is one of the biggest zoos in Europe. There is an old castle from the late 17th century in the northeast of the Tierpar

voyage.name: Stasi Museum
voyage.content: This museum describes the procedures applied by the East German secret police. Every Friday to Monday, there is a guided tour in English at 15:00 (5€).

voyage.name: Gedenkstätte Hohenschönhausen
voyage.hours: Daily English-speaking tour between July 1st and November 14th, 14:30
voyage.content: Experience the Stasi Secret Police Prison first-hand. Tours are compulsory. Some of the tours are done by former inmates.

voyage.name: Museum Karlshorst
voyage.content: In this house the surrender of Germany was signed on May 9th, 1945, ending WWII in Europe. This museum describes the history of the war between Germany and the Soviet Union between 1941 and 1945 and the GDR/German-Russian relationship ever since. Historic rooms, permanent exhibition and special exhibits.

voyage.name: Mies van der Rohe Haus
voyage.price: exhibitions are free, guided tours ca €5
voyage.content: The last Mies van der Rohe building (a dwelling house) in Germany before his emigration to the U.S. (1938). Now there are small contemporary/modern art exhibitions.

voyage.name: Victoriastadt
voyage.content: A relatively well and completely retained (at least by Berlin standards) 19th century residential quarter. Partly under renovation. Of note are six buildings first (1875) built of concrete - but you can't make out a difference from the outside.

voyage.name: Weißensee cemetery
voyage.content: The second largest Jewish cemetery in Europe.

voyage.name: World's Garden
voyage.price: Entrance is €4 in winter and €7 in summer
voyage.hours: Apr-Sep: daily 09:00-20:00; Mar and Oct: daily 09:00-18:00; Nov-Feb: daily 09:00-16:00. Guided tours take place on Wed Thu Fri every 30 min from 10:30 until 12:30
voyage.content: Inside you can find a large and well-established Chinese garden, a Korean garden, a small Bali garden/glasshouse, an Oriental garden with nice fountains and a cloister and a Japanese garden which is a project by the city partnership of Berlin and Tokyo. The latter has been built by Zen priests. Although quite crowded at times, there are not that many tourists so here's a chance to brush up on your German skills. As t

voyage.name: Gründerzeitmuseum
voyage.hours: Wed and Sun 10:00-18:00; tours outside of opening hours can be arranged
voyage.content: Features many objects and even whole rooms in Wilhelminian style. Only accessible by guided tour (English tours can be arranged).

voyage.name: Schloss and Schlosspark Biesdorf
voyage.content: A small castle in late classical style. It was built 1868 by Martin Gropius (uncle of the Bauhaus-founder and other architects, the von Siemens family changed the castle a bit around 1900 and they enlarged the dimensions of the park, which is today renovated and nice to wander around when the sun is shining. Located within a few minutes' walking distance from Biesdorf station (take the S5 from the city centre) or Els

voyage.name: Windmill
voyage.content: One of the few windmills in Berlin is located in Marzahn. After registration one can visit it and have a look at the functions of the windmill. To get there, take the S7 or S75 until "Springpfuhl" station, then the tram 8 or M18 until "Alt-Marzahn".

voyage.name: Zentralfriedhof Friedrichsfelde
voyage.content: The cemetery is also known as the Memorial to the Socialists. It has many interesting monuments and graves of known people.

voyage.name: Galerie M
voyage.content: Varying exhibitions.

voyage.name: Schönhausen Palace
voyage.content: A pretty restored Baroque palace (restoration completed in 2009).

voyage.name: Harness racing
voyage.hours: Usually the races take place on Sundays
voyage.content: There is a harness racing track in Karlshorst.

voyage.name: Kienberg
voyage.content: Before or after visiting the "Gardens of the World", tourists might be interested in climbing on top of the Kienberg (a small hill nearby with a view on the surrounding suburbs) or to go for a walk in the valley of the Wuhle (a small river). More information on the area can be found on the district's official website (in German).

voyage.name: IGA Cable Car
voyage.price: Return ticket €6.50 (it is not part of the BVG fare system)
voyage.content: A cable car built for the international gardening exhibition in 2017 which remained in operation afterwards.

voyage.name: Brotfabrik
voyage.content: This institution, literally the "bread factory" has been converted into a cultural space hosting various theater, cinema and art events

voyage.name: Former Silent Cinema Delphi
voyage.content: This former cinema has become a theatre.

voyage.name: Eastgate Berlin
voyage.content: About 150 shops, restaurants, etc. Close by is an entertainment centre with cinemas etc.

voyage.name: Helle Mitte
voyage.content: A smaller shopping centre.

voyage.name: Spree Center
voyage.content: Small shopping centre.

voyage.name: Tierpark Bistro
voyage.content: Has some of the best Doener in the Berlin area. They have a great neighbourhood feel, and delicious Middle Eastern food in the German style.

voyage.name: La Paz
voyage.content: Mexican restaurant and bar, in the summer you can sit outside in the adjacent pedestrian area. Good food and friendly service.

voyage.name: J.A.S.
voyage.content: Schnitzel, chicken, salads, asparagus when in season. Free freifunk internet.

voyage.name: Bistro am Schloßpark
voyage.content: This Biergarten is simple, but friendly and a convenient place to have a beer and a currywurst after visiting the castle.

voyage.name: Kulturhaus Kili
voyage.content: Alternative reggae, dancehall and goa techno club, but also theater and art events.

voyage.name: Sisyphos
voyage.content: This techno club is located in a former factory for dog biscuits in Berlin's Rummelsburg neighborhood. It has two indoor dance floors and a large open-air area.

voyage.name: Void
voyage.content: Techno club within an old electrical transformer station with a focus on drum 'n' bass, techno, house, progressive and psytrance.

voyage.name: A&O Hotel and Hostel Berlin Kolumbus
Hotel Helle Mitte
voyage.content: Modern but affordable middle-class hotel.

voyage.name: Etap Berlin Ost
voyage.content: Typical low budget hotel managed by the Accor group.

voyage.name: Park Hotel Schloss Kaulsdorf
voyage.content: Probably the only luxurious hotel in the area, in a small castle.

voyage.name: Youth hostel Pro-social
voyage.price: One night in a four-person apartment €12. Up to three night stay €14. Breakfast €3.50
voyage.content: 153 beds in rooms of 1 to 4 beds, all have sofa/living area, separate shower and WC, and small entrance hall.

voyage.name: Wannsee
voyage.content: This is the number-one bathing and recreation spot in western Berlin, with several beaches, the large Strandbad Wannsee open-air lido and several historic landmarks nearby.

voyage.name: Bierpinsel
voyage.content: The Bierpinsel ("beer brush") is a building in Steglitz which resembles an observation tower and is famous for its pop-art appearance. The futuristic building was built from 1972 to 1976 and has since been used as restaurant, night club, bar, radio station and art café. Once threatened with demolition as a white elephant, this unique structure was instead landmarked and is well worth looking at.

voyage.name: Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin-Dahlem
voyage.alt: Botanischer Garten und Botanisches Museum Berlin-Dahlem
voyage.hours: Jan 09:00-16:00; Feb 09:00-17:00; Mar 09:00-18:00; Apr 09:00-20:00; May-Jul 09:00-21:00; Aug 09:00-20:00; Sep 09:00-19:00; Oct 09:00-18:00; Nov-Dec 09:00-16:00; greenhouses close one hour earlier than the overall closing time
voyage.content: These beautiful gardens, which include 6,000 square metres of greenhouse space and over 20,000 plants spread over 42 hectares, are part of the Free University of Berlin. The museum is closed till 2027 for a complete redesign and renovation.

voyage.name: Jagdschloss Grunewald
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar: Sat Sun holidays 10:00-16:00; Apr-Oct: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00
voyage.content: Built in 1542. An impressive traditional country estate with stately architecture, it is an enclave of untouched regional cultural history and architectonic epochs. The 80-hectare mixed forest also provides a wide network of paths for walking and rambling.

voyage.name: Mexikoplatz
voyage.content: Heritage listed Art Nouveau railway station and charming surrounding city square.

voyage.name: Schloss und Schlosspark Glienicke
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Tue-Sun; Mar Nov-Dec: Sat Sun holidays
voyage.content: This castle is one of Berlin's oldest castles and where Prince Carl used to reside. Be sure to check out Glienicke Bridge, the bridge that became renowned for the exchange of Western and Eastern secret agents. You can also visit Glienicke Park.

voyage.name: Strandbad Wannsee
voyage.content: This heritage-protected public bathing beach which opened in 1907 is one of the largest inland lidos in Europe and has a 1275-m-long sand beach, a capacity for up to 30,000 guests and a popular nudist area.

voyage.name: Steinstücken
voyage.content: This would be a perfectly ordinary neighbourhood of Berlin or perhaps neighbouring Potsdam visible only on maps that show the border between Berlin and Potsdam if not for its history. While the Berlin border during German partition included a number of enclaves and exclaves, this is the only place where a significant number (some 300 people) ended up on an "island" of West Berlin surrounded by East German territory.

voyage.name: Helmholtz-Zentrum Nuclear Reactor
voyage.content: The 10 MW research reactor BER II delivers neutron beams for a wide range of scientific investigations. On open house day, interested visitors are allowed to take guided tours through the experimental halls around the research reactor. Scientists and reactor experts will be there on these days to answer questions about the facility and the safety measures.

voyage.name: Allied Museum
voyage.content: A museum showing the Western side of the Cold War.

voyage.name: Brücke-Museum
voyage.content: Works from the Dresden art collaborative called "Die Brücke".

voyage.name: House of the Wannsee Conference
voyage.hours: Daily 10:00-18:00; closed May 1, Good Fri, Jan 1, Dec 24-Dec 26, Dec 31
voyage.content: This museum explains how this house was used for a meeting of senior Nazis to ensure that they all knew that the SS would industrialize the use of mass-murder in disposing of Jews and "undesirables" and to debate a little the logistics of the Holocaust, for which Hitler had already given the orders.

voyage.name: Liebermann-Villa am Wannsee
voyage.hours: Oct-Mar: Wed-Mon 11:00-17:00; Apr-Sep: Wed-Mon 10:00-18:00, Thu Sun holidays 10:00-19:00; closed Dec 24, Dec 31 off
voyage.content: House museum on Max Liebermann, German painter and printmaker. Has about 15 Lieberman paintings.

voyage.name: Museum of European Cultures
voyage.content: The biggest of its sort in Europe. At the museum district of Dahlem.

voyage.name: Museumsdorf Düppel
voyage.hours: 14 March – 1 November: Sat-Sun and holidays except on Wed, 10:00-18:00
voyage.content: This museum is perhaps something you wouldn't expect in a major metropolis and truth be told it owes its existence in part to partition (when West Berlin schoolkids couldn't go to the surrounding Brandenburg countryside to experience rural life). Opened in 1975, it is an attempt to recreate as faithfully as feasible a medieval farming village from roughly the era of Berlin's founding (12th or 13th century). The villa

voyage.name: Boulevard Berlin
voyage.content: An indoor shopping mall.

voyage.name: Forum Steglitz
voyage.content: Forum Steglitz, another indoor shopping mall, has much of the same stores that the earlier Das Schloss boasts, although the ice cream shop on one of the upper floors is a great place to take a break. They even have seating out front when the weather is nice. There is a nice, inexpensive make-up shop on the first floor to the left when you enter.

voyage.name: Karstadt
voyage.content: Karstadt is a nice department store with a grocery store in the basement where you can find some hard to find food items.

voyage.name: Das Naturkaufhaus
voyage.content: The largest natural department store in the city, featuring eco-friendly clothes, paper products and beauty products, among other things. The best part is the basement, which is full of interesting decorations and cool items.

voyage.name: Peek & Cloppenberg
voyage.content: A branch of the department store.

voyage.name: Das Schloss
voyage.content: An upscale indoor shopping mall with a creative ceiling decoration.

voyage.name: Schloss Straßen Center
voyage.content: The Schloss Straßen Center, another indoor shopping mall, is often packed with people coming out with brown Primark bags as this is the shopping centre which boasts Berlin's first Primark.

voyage.name: Werken, Spielen, Schenken
voyage.content: A great place for kids. With a toy store in the front and a craft store in the back, you will find everything you need for playing or crafting.

voyage.name: Confiserie Reichert
voyage.content: A classic pastry place and café that also makes fabulous ice cream sundaes, many of them laced with wine or liqueurs. Also serves savory food. The price is a bit elevated, but so is the experience. Beautiful exterior, too.

voyage.name: Curry Wolf Steglitz
voyage.content: Nice currywurst snack bar.

voyage.name: Die Fischerhütte am Schlachtensee
voyage.content: A cozy, yet elegant high end restaurant with an impressive visible wine collection. Sit outside in the warmer months for the gorgeous views outside.

voyage.name: Loretta am Wannsee
voyage.content: One of the most popular beer gardens in Berlin in summer, for eating and drinking in the sun. There is a Loretta restaurant, the Loretta Biergarten and the Loretta Almhütte.

voyage.name: Yangguofu Malatang Steglitz
voyage.price: Cost is by weight of the items you choose: €3.19 per 100 grams; two people can share a huge bowl for €40
voyage.content: The Berlin location of a fast-casual chain based in China that specializes in spicy soups (malatang) but also makes a non-spicy tomato broth and sesame-based dry mix. You choose the other ingredients from the refrigerator in the front of the restaurant, and they are of high quality and include interesting items like spicy Thai fishcakes and buckwheat noodles that you might not find at other locations. Extensive indoo

voyage.name: Café Melanie
voyage.content: Have a coffee, long drink or cocktail at this cozy café which is one of the most longstanding in Steglitz and Friedenau. This venue also offers some delicious meals, ice cream, breakfast and brunch.

voyage.name: Hotel Pension Enzian
voyage.content: A friendly, family-run hotel with large double bed rooms. Small hotel with a personal atmosphere. Within 1-minute walking distance is a S-Bahn station and a good Spanish restaurant. Serves breakfast, wireless is €4 per day.

voyage.name: Landhaus Schlachtensee
voyage.content: Set nearby the Schlachtensee and Krumme Lanke lakes, the Landhaus offers a quiet and tranquil location, with the personalized service of a bed and breakfast.

voyage.name: Tempelhof Airport
voyage.price: The park is free; guided tour of the building €15 for adults, €10 for students, €7 for children 14 and under
voyage.content: The "mother of all airports", according to Sir Norman Foster, is a huge relic of the interwar era. The terminal building, built between 1936 and 1941 immediately south of the city centre, was the hot spot of the Berlin airlift (Berliner Luftbrücke) in 1948-49, but closed as an airport on October 30, 2008. In 1951 a monument was added to its entrance square - then renamed "Airlift Square" -to commemorate the airlifts

voyage.name: Police Historical Collection
voyage.content: Official website (in German). A museum of Berlin's different police forces through the ages, displaying historic uniforms, weapons, and specialist equipment such as cameras. Completing the collection are a photo archive and around 50 police vehicles, which are only viewable on certain 'open doors' days.

voyage.name: Schwerbelastungskörper
voyage.hours: Tue-Wed 14:00-18:00; Thu 10:00-18:00; Sun 13:00-16:00. Closed Nov-Mar and Good Fri
voyage.content: From 1941, 12,000 tons of concrete in a 15-m-high and 20-m-diameter cylinder were built to test the load-bearing capacity of the Berlin soils (turns out glacial sands are no good basis for gargantuan architecture) for Albert Speer's Germania buildings. Too massive for later blasting, this is one of the more bizarre remains of the Third Reich.

voyage.name: Sonnenallee
voyage.content: Became famous from the film named after this street. During the Cold War, the street was split, with one section belonging to East Berlin and one to West Berlin.

voyage.name: Neuköllner Oper
voyage.content: Visit a play and be amazed by the creativity, which the opera house has won some awards for.

voyage.name: Stadtbad Neukölln
voyage.content: Built from 1912-14 in Art Nouveau style and carefully renovated in 1984, this swimming pool (actually two in one building), covered in mosaics and domes, is one of Berlin's most beautiful. A must see for architecture fans.

voyage.name: Volkspark Mariendorf
voyage.content: Boasts an open-air cinema and is the great to go to at night.

voyage.name: Britzer Garten
voyage.content: A 90-hectare garden and former national garden show place (1984); public park with great flora and big playgrounds for kids; popular amongst children and seniors on weekends.

voyage.name: Kindl-Boulevard Passage
voyage.content: Shopping centre on Hermanstraße with many stores, a cinema, and a Kaiser's supermarket.

voyage.name: Neukölln Arkaden
voyage.content: An abundance of clothing stores and eateries, a post office, gym, a cinema known as "Karli" (movies in both German and Turkish shown regularly), and a very large supermarket (Kaufland) in the basement. Free wi-fi.

voyage.name: Turkish Market
voyage.content: The “Turk's market” at the Landwehr Canal at the Maybachufer in Neukölln near Kreuzberg sells vegetables, Turkish specialities and a lot of materials.

voyage.name: Gropiusstadt Passagen
voyage.content: It's the biggest mall in Berlin and offers a wide variety of shops.

voyage.name: Cafe & Restaurant Louis
voyage.content: Austrian food, giant schnitzels and quality beer on tap.

voyage.name: Café Jacques
voyage.content: Great French cuisine (especially the fish and the self-made noodles), nice service, very crowded though.

voyage.name: Cafe Rix
voyage.content: Next to the Neukölln Opera house with international cuisine.

voyage.name: Tabibito
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant, family-run, very friendly (sometimes you get a snack for free), since it's little, can be very crowded in the evenings.

voyage.name: TanzCafé Britz
voyage.price: €3.90 and up, items over €10 are rare
voyage.content: Hidden away in a residential area. Cute café/restaurant with lots of dancing activities and excellent and really cheap food prepared by a French chef.

voyage.name: Café Selig
voyage.content: Cute café/restaurant in the Schillerkiez by the church. Good place to people-watch, drink a coffee, and to eat brunch.

voyage.name: Zio Felix
voyage.content: Good pizza.

voyage.name: Britzer Mühle
voyage.content: Classical German cuisine in an old wind mill.

voyage.name: Casa Montella
voyage.content: Good Italian restaurant in Rudow.

voyage.name: Arcaoda
voyage.content: This club in an old bowling alley offers electro club nights, live music performances, independent music, art exhibitions and food.

voyage.name: Brauhaus Rixdorf
voyage.content: Traditional brewery with a very nice biergarten, lovely in summer. The food is typical Bavarian fare, and of pretty good quality.

voyage.name: Klunkerkranich
voyage.content: Popular rooftop club, beach bar, sundeck or garden on top of a parking garage with a fantastic view over Neukölln. Generous indoor space and even more outdoor. Live music and DJs playing electro, funk, disco or jazz.Takes a little effort to find, once you have located the shopping centre victory is within sight. This is a very relaxed spot.

voyage.name: Kulturverein Kinski
voyage.content: Famous for late nights and cultural activities. Frequented by Neukölln film enthusiasts, and occasionally rare films are screened. A nice feature: if you want to organise an artistic event or plan to DJ, just go there and sign up in the list at the bar.

voyage.name: Frollein Langner
voyage.content: Furnished with several sofas it has a living room atmosphere. They serve Bavarian beer and small snacks. The main room is non-smoking. There is a separate room for smokers.

voyage.name: Froschkönig Pianobar
voyage.content: Awesome pianobar with literature nights and occasional jazz concerts. Very relaxed atmosphere, located in the Schillerkiez.

voyage.name: Syndikat
voyage.content: One of the most famous bars in this part of town. It's been around for some 25 years and considered to be one of the best 'Kneipen' in Neukölln.

voyage.name: 2A-Hostel
voyage.content: Cheap modern hostel, built in 2011.

voyage.name: Estrel
voyage.content: It claims to be biggest hotel and entertainment complex in Europe. 1,125 rooms, a convention center and Michael Jackson's father stayed here.

voyage.name: Mercure Hotel Tempelhof Airport
voyage.content: East of the former airport.

voyage.name: Aerodynamic Park
voyage.content: This aeronautical experimental park on the grounds of Germany's first air field Johannisthal consists of a group of several individual technical monuments such as the walkable Großer Windkanal (High-speed wind channel, 1932–34), the Trudelturm (Fatty tower), a vertical wind tunnel for spinning tests (1934–36), the Schallgedämpfter Motorenprüfstand (Sound-insulated engine test bed, 1933–35) and the Isothermische Kugel

voyage.name: Regattastrecke Berlin-Grünau
voyage.content: The 2000-m-long regatta course at the Langer See lake in Grünau was an official site of the Olympic Games 1936. The first rowing regatta took place here on 27 June 1880.

voyage.name: Seebad Wendenschloss
voyage.content: This public lido at Langer See which opened in 1915 offers a pleasant sand beach, an art exhibition, beach volleyball courts and a fantastic view onto the regatta course on the other shore.

voyage.name: Nazi Forced Labor Documentation Center
voyage.price: free, guided tours are available on request
voyage.content: The Schöneweide forced labor camp (GBI-Lager 75/76) on Britzer Straße is a complete ensemble, which makes it a rather unusual site in Berlin. Of the original thirteen housing barracks erected between 1943 and 1945, eleven are still standing today. Six barracks on the western part of the former camp grounds belong to the Documentation Center on Nazi Forced Labor.

voyage.name: Archenhold Observatory
voyage.hours: Museum: Wed-Sun 14:00-16:30. Guided tours: Thu 20:00; Sat Sun 15:00
voyage.content: The longest moving refracting telescope is 21 m long with a lens diameter of 68 cm. This giant telescope was built in 1896 by Dr. Friedrich Simon Archenhold but is now part of the Deutsches Technikmuseum Berlin. It was the place where Albert Einstein presented his Theory of Relativity to the public in 1915.

voyage.name: Soviet War Memorial
voyage.content: In Treptower Park, a huge memorial and the surrounding war cemetery for 5,000 of the Red Army soldiers fallen during the Battle of Berlin. Distinctive Soviet realism features, with its iconic statue of a Red Army soldier standing proudly over a broken Nazi swastika.

voyage.name: Spreepark
voyage.content: This abandoned amusement park with its iconic large Ferris wheel opened in the German Democratic Republic in 1969. After its closing in 2002 the rotting theme park and its apocalyptic atmosphere became a target of international media coverage, amongst others by the New York Times. In 2016 it was announced that the venue will be restored and reopened as an art and culture park.

voyage.name: Altstadt Köpenick
voyage.content: The old town of Köpenick is surrounded by water. Especially noteworthy are the Köpenick Palace which houses a museum of applied art and the Neogothic town hall.

voyage.name: Schloss Köpenick
voyage.content: The charming Baroque water palace of the Hohenzollern electors surrounded by the Dahme river and an English garden.

voyage.name: Museum of Decorative Arts
voyage.content: In the Köpenick Palace.

voyage.name: Berliner Bürgerbräu
voyage.content: The building of one of Berlin’s oldest breweries is a ravishingly beautiful and heritage-protected industrial monument.

voyage.name: Spreetunnel Friedrichshagen
voyage.content: This heritage-protected 120-m-long pedestrian tunnel below the river Spree was the first ferro-concrete tunnel in Germany that has been built using pneumatic caissons. Two beaches can be accessed via the tunnel which are not far from its south entrance.

voyage.name: Kleiner Müggelsee
voyage.content: The "Small Müggelsee" is southeast of the "Large Müggelsee". Its sloping sand beach, which is called Strandbad Kleiner Müggelsee is one of the most popular bathing beaches in this southeast corner of Berlin, if not the most popular.

voyage.name: Müggelsee
voyage.content: Berlin's biggest lake and popular resort for bathing and watersports. You can also travel there by tram, which is an experience by itself.

voyage.name: Müggelturm
voyage.content: An observation tower without an elevator in Southeast Berlin, from which you can see that there is a great deal of forest around Berlin. There is a cafe at the tower.

voyage.name: Neuvenedig
voyage.content: A beautiful landscape of water canals and vegetation with charming little fish restaurants.

voyage.name: Treptower Park
voyage.content: Nice and clean park next to the Spree. Famous for the Insel der Jugend (Isle of Youth) and its numerous boat rentals and boat trips.

voyage.name: FEZ Berlin
voyage.content: While the former Palast der Republik in Berlin-Mitte has been demolished in favor of the reconstruction of the Berliner Schloss, its counterpart for kids, pupils and "young pioneers", the Pionierpalast Ernst Thälmann can still be seen at the Volkspark Wuhlheide. The large building complex which was built from 1976 to 1979 is a contemporary testimony for architecture in the socialist German Democratic Republic and of

voyage.name: Kindl-Bühne Wuhlheide
voyage.address: Strasse zum FEZ 4 (An der Wuhlheide), Berlin-Oberschöneweide
voyage.content: The Kindl-Bühne Wuhlheide is a cultural heritage site and of Berlin's largest and most popular open-air stages for rock, pop and electronic concerts in the shape of an ancient amphitheater.

voyage.name: Badeschiff
voyage.content: An old cargo ship hull converted to a fresh-water swimming pool, anchored permanently on the river Spree. Provides a nice opportunity to swim on the Spree, without swimming in the river, which is far too polluted. There is a bar with disco DJ music next to the pool. In winter time, the pool is covered against the weather.

voyage.name: Union Filmtheater
voyage.content: This is an ancient cinema which opened in 1913 in a former ballroom. After World War II it was repaired improvisationally and only had one cinema hall, but today it has 3 modernized halls and also offers a bar, a bistro and a bookable dance hall for parties. Independent and kid's movies.

voyage.name: Fähre F24
voyage.hours: May-October 11:00-19:00, crosses the river as often as needed
voyage.content: Make a crossing with the only human-powered ferry run by Berlin's public transport company BVG. The F24 is operated with a rowing boat, and you can use your valid BVG ticket or buy a ticket on site. It needs 12 strokes of an oar to cross the Müggelspree river.

voyage.name: Go on the water
voyage.content: Rent a motor boat, rowing boat, canoe or kayak and explore the Müggelspree, Dahme, Müggelsee, Langer See, Seddinsee or Dämeritzsee and the various channels which connect these waters.

voyage.name: Strandbad Müggelsee
voyage.content: The history of this heritage-protected public bathing beach at Müggelsee traces back to the 1910s. It has a more than 500 meters long beach and a capacity for 25,000 guests.

voyage.name: Woltersdorfer Straßenbahn
voyage.content: Local independent tram route which for many years was one of the last in Germany to still use East German four-wheeled tramcars built between 1957 and 1961, but has finally acquired modern low-floor cars. For special occasions, some still run along with even older trams. The line is 5.6 km long and operates daily as it is still a public transit service. The tramway is line 87 in the VBB fare system, and VBB tickets v

voyage.name: Winzerfest Köpenick
voyage.content: An open-air event in the old town of Köpenick that takes place every year for a weekend once in spring (around end of April) and once in summer (around August). Wineries from (mostly) Germany bring their wine which you get to enjoy at a moderate price. There are also food stalls.

voyage.name: Forum Köpenick
voyage.content: Large and modern shopping center which houses 140 shops as well as restaurants, dentists and a post office.

voyage.name: Kaufland Berlin-Adlershof
voyage.content: While Adlershof is no tourist destination per se, you might arrive at Germany's largest science and business compound WISTA when you are a student, visiting researcher or businessman. This large supermarket on two floors is a good place to buy food supplies for your trips and excursions to southern Berlin.

voyage.name: Park Center Treptow
voyage.content: Shopping centre which houses about 50 shops, services and a pharmacy.

voyage.name: Treptower Hallentrödelmarkt
voyage.content: Huge indoor flea market

voyage.name: Zentrum Schöneweide
voyage.content: Shopping centre at the S-Bahn station Schöneweide which houses about 30 shops, services, a pharmacy, a Media Markt consumer electronics discounter and some restaurants and bistros.

voyage.name: Blaue Lagune
voyage.content: A coffeeshop/restaurant where you can have great coffee, house-made excellent ice cream and cakes, and great food from a short but just as excellent menu, and all that in a wonderful ambiente. Nestled in a corner of Johannisthal, part of Schoeneweide, which is a subsection of Treptow.

voyage.name: Klipper
voyage.content: This firmly anchored restaurant ship is certainly one of the most beautiful venues for having dinner in Treptow and Berlin.

voyage.name: Luise Restaurant and Bar
voyage.content: Friendly service, delicious German/Italian food and a great view over the Dahme and the Spree both from inside and outside on the big wooden terrace.

voyage.name: Müggelseefischerei
voyage.content: This fishery right next to the ferry terminal offers fresh and smoked fish caught in Müggelsee since more than 35 years.

voyage.name: Neu Helgoland
voyage.content: One of Berlin's most beautiful waterside restaurants with over 100 years of tradition. Regular events such as concerts and comedy, often with popular East German bands. Locals usually arrive by boat.

voyage.name: Rübezahl
voyage.content: This waterside restaurant with beer garden named after the folklore mountain spirit is one of the best-known and oldest at Müggelsee and offers delicious meals, dinner events, weddings and an ice skating rink in winter. The food is good but on the pricey side and they make you pay to use the toilets.

voyage.name: Schmetterlingshorst
voyage.content: This history of this cozy pub for hikers, sportsmen and day-trippers at Langer See and its butterfly collection can be traced back to the year 1898.

voyage.name: Westernrestaurant Richtershorn am See
voyage.content: Old style Western restaurant at the waterside with a log cabin, outdoor terrace, dancehall, wharf, zoo and winter garden as well as a beautiful view over the Langer See lake.

voyage.name: Dresdner Feinbäckerei
voyage.content: This tradition-rich confectionery and café which was founded in 1906 offers backed goods, cookies and cakes from Saxony as well as coffee. Regular events such as readings take place at the café.

voyage.name: Köpenick Palace Cafe
voyage.hours: Nov-Mar: Thu-Sun 10:00-18:00; Oct-Apr: Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-23:00
voyage.content: Both inside and outside are beautiful places to have a glass of wine or beer or a cup of coffee with a whipped cream cake. Also have menus for lunch and dinner.

voyage.name: Arena Club
voyage.content: This techno club in a raw and run-down old boiler room of 500 m² provides the perfect atmosphere for hard industrial techno. It has one dance floor and two bars and an impressive light installation at the ceiling. Next to the club, the huge Arena Berlin compound also includes a larger multipurpose hall of 6,500 m² which hosts events such as concerts, fashion shows and conventions, a glass house for further events and

voyage.name: Club der Visionäre
voyage.content: Atmospheric club at the waterside well-known for minimal techno, house and techno-house and high-grade DJ bookings. Originally only a summer venue, it now also has an indoor winter location at the MS Hoppetosse excursion ship which is docked nearby.

voyage.name: Else
voyage.content: Open-air techno club and beer garden at the Elsenbrücke bridge which is made out of shipping containers and has a wooden floor and stage and a large sound system. Subsidiary of the Wilde Renate club.

voyage.name: Freiheit Fünfzehn
voyage.content: Club location and beautiful beer garden at the waterside in Köpenick. The party area includes a concert location on a former cargo ship on the water, a dance club called Pop.arty and a bar called Duke bar.

voyage.name: Freischwimmer
voyage.content: Bar at the river on a ponton with good food and drinks, good for chilling.

voyage.name: Haus Zenner
voyage.content: Restaurant with beer garden and live music venue where Jazz and Swing bands perform regularly. It is one of the successors of the legendary Eierschale Jazz club which was located in Berlin-Dahlem from 1956 to 2000.

voyage.name: Hoppetosse
voyage.content: This is a club for minimal techno and house located on a permanently docked excursion ship on the Spree river, the MS Hoppetosse. It is the winter venue for the Club der Visionäre. It has one dance floor and a Martion Bullfrog sound system.

voyage.name: Insel Berlin
voyage.content: Club on the Insel der Jugend island on the Spree river with three floors, music varies from reggae to techno to indie to gothic.

voyage.name: Rummelsburg
voyage.content: Techno festivals, raves and beach bars right at the waterside and the old Rummelsburg power plant.

voyage.name: Dorint Hotel Berlin Adlershof
voyage.content: This hotel is recommended for researchers and businessmen visiting the science and business compound WISTA in Adlershof. But note that it usually takes around 45 minutes from here to the inner city (Berlin East) by using public transport.

voyage.name: Hotel Müggelsee Berlin
voyage.content: This conference and wellness hotel with 172 rooms at the Müggelsee is embedded by woodland and parks. This hotel is recommended for nature lovers and sports fans who want to discover the Müggelsee and the surrounding lakes and take time out from the trouble of the city.

voyage.name: Charlottenburg Palace
voyage.content: One of the oldest buildings in Charlottenburg and actually the reason for the whole city to be built.

voyage.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
voyage.content: Also known as "der hohle Zahn" (the Hollow Tooth), this church in Breitscheidplatz is a memorial to Kaiser Wilhelm, and one of Berlin's most famous landmarks. Thick walls and plain decor mark it as neo-Romanesque, but with what's left of the Gedächtniskirche, it's tough to distinguish it as any one style. Allied bombing left only one tower standing on 22 November 1943, but a new location for worship designed by Egon

voyage.name: Museum of Photography
voyage.content: Admission €8, discounted €4, young people up to the age of 18 free. Guided tours every Th 18:00 and Su 16:00.

voyage.name: Käthe Kollwitz Museum
voyage.content: Käthe Kollwitz's reputation as a social activist who used art as a means to express her support of pacifism was hard-won. Her son was killed in the World War I, after which her art took a turn for the morose. When her grandson was killed in World War II, her art became even darker and more brooding as she contemplated the huge loss of life Germany had suffered. Her own losses and those of the nation affected her art.

voyage.name: The Story of Berlin
voyage.hours: Closed for construction as of April 2024
voyage.content: A multimedia museum documenting Berlin's history. You can also visit an underground bunker with room for over 3000 people.

voyage.name: Museum Berggruen
voyage.content: Also known as "Picasso und seine Zeit", this not so large, but precious museum hosts a very good collection of paintings and sculptures signed by Picasso, Klee, Matisse, Giacometti, and others from the first decades of the 20th century.

voyage.name: Bröhan Museum
voyage.content: A small but interesting collection of decorative arts from the Art Nouveau and Art Deco periods

voyage.name: Collection Scharf-Gerstenberg
voyage.price: Admission Museum Berggruen + Sammlung Scharf-Gerstenberg: €10, discounted: €5, young people up to the age of 18 free
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to surrealist art.

voyage.name: Savignyplatz
voyage.content: Small park in the heart of West Berlin. Great place to chill on a sunny day. There are many great cafés and restaurants nearby. Linger over a coffee here and watch people passing by.

voyage.name: Berlin sculpture
voyage.content: Once part of the Skulpturenbulevard project, this sculpture was made for the 750th anniversary of Berlin (in 1987). It consists of four steel tubes looping but not touching each other, symbolizing the division of the city.

voyage.name: Plötzensee Memorial Center
voyage.content: An eerie memorial to victims of the Nazi regime built on the place of a former execution room, where nearly 2,900 people were put to death between 1933 and 1945.

voyage.name: Olympiastadion
voyage.content: Built by Hitler for the 1936 Olympic Games, this is one of the better examples of Nazi neoclassical architecture (laying claim to the legacy of Rome, fasces and all) and is still used for sporting events. At those Olympics, African-American athlete Jesse Owens won four gold medals, a party-spoiler for Aryan superiority. It's the home of soccer team Hertha BSC - they were relegated in 2023 and now play in 2. Bundeslig

voyage.name: Berliner Funkturm und Messehallen
voyage.hours: Tower viewing platform: Mon 10:00–20:00, Tue–Sun 10:00–23:00, limited access during trade fairs
voyage.content: 150 m high lattice tower with open-air observation deck 124 m above ground.

voyage.name: Haus des Rundfunks
voyage.content: Designed by Hans Poelzig in 1929, it is the first self-contained broadcasting house in the world and it is still in use today.

voyage.name: Unité d'Habitation
voyage.content: The building by Le Corbusier from 1957 stands close to the stadium. You can see a building that influenced the way modern residential blocks are designed all over the world.

voyage.name: Georg Kolbe Museum
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to the Berliner sculptor.

voyage.name: Christi-Auferstehungs-Kathedrale
voyage.alt: Russian Orthodox cathedral of the Resurrection of Jesus

voyage.name: Rheingauviertel
voyage.content: at the Rüdesheimer Platz

voyage.name: Grunewaldturm
voyage.content: Historic observation tower in the forest near the big Havel River.

voyage.name: Teufelsberg
voyage.content: A man-made hill of about 120 m in the Grunewald, created after the Second World War from debris of the city. On top is the Field Station Berlin, a former US listening station. Inside the building complex you can see lots of graffiti art. The hill can be accessed without any restrictions and is free; however, the building complex is surrounded by fences and requires a ticket (tours are available as well).

voyage.name: Akazien-/Goltzstraße
voyage.content: Restaurants abound here, with cuisines ranging from Afghan to Nepalese and Thai, plus several pizzerias and sandwich places. Prices are low, especially compared with other locations in the tourist centre of Berlin. Around Eisenacher Straße (extension of Goltzstr.) you’ll find even more bars and cafés situated in the basements of nice old houses. During World War II, this part of Berlin was not destroyed by bombs as m

voyage.name: Bayerischer Platz
voyage.content: The Bayerischer Platz is the centre of the Bayerisches Viertel ("Bavarian district", with many streets named after Bavarian cities), which was destroyed a lot more during World War II (about 60%). Somewhere around there Albert Einstein lived once. You’ll find several memorial signs providing information about the Nazi regime's persecution of gays and Jews.

voyage.name: Nollendorfplatz
voyage.content: This area was Gay Central during the Weimar Republic, and it is today. But of course all are welcome. There is a diverse mix of restaurants and stores, several of which are open till midnight or later every day. The U-Bahn station has a superstructure and towers that echo the appearance of the Art Nouveau Neues Schauspielhaus across the street, now the Metropol, where radical left-wing dramas used to be presented in

voyage.name: Planetarium am Insulaner
voyage.content: In the very southeast of Schöneberg, there are daily shows for children and grown-ups alike. Projection is into a drawn Berlin skyline. Several guided tours to the obervatory daily with sky observation, conditions permitting.

voyage.name: Rathaus Schöneberg
voyage.content: The district town hall was the main town hall for West Berlin during the Cold War. The freedom bell (a present from the American people) and several memorials from that time can be found here. On the main balcony in 1963 U.S. President John F. Kennedy made his famous statement, "All free men, wherever they may live, are citizens of Berlin, and, therefore, as a free man, I take pride in the words ‘Ich bin ein Berliner

voyage.name: Viktoria Luise Platz
voyage.content: Features a nice fountain, stately old houses and a good night time hot spot. Many people hang out in the platz in good weather.

voyage.name: Winterfeldplatz
voyage.content: Places with markets on Wednesdays and Saturdays are popular with locals at Winterfeldplatz. Buy a coffee and browse amongst the stalls; this is a place to unearth hidden gems. Breakfast is served usually until 14:00-15:00.

voyage.name: Hamburger Bahnhof – Museum für Gegenwart
voyage.price: €10, concession €5, under 18 years free. Free entry for everyone every first Thursday of the month from 16:00-20:00
voyage.content: Museum of Contemporary Art located in former Hamburger Bahnhof train station. Big halls filled with artworks made since 1960s. In 2004 Rieckhallen, former Lehrter Bahnhof, was opened and now provides exhibition space for the Friedrich Christian Flick Collection. Free public guided tours (in English): Sa and Su at 12:00.

voyage.name: Moabit Prison Historical Park
voyage.hours: Summer: daily until 21:00; winter: daily until 18:00
voyage.content: A former prison built around 1850 with a haunting history until after the end of World War II (around 1955). During WWII it was used by the Nazis for oppression, torture and murder of political opponents. Nowadays it is a public park serving as a memorial.

voyage.name: Buchstabenmuseum
voyage.content: Like the name says, this museum showcases letters that have been used in signage as well as entire signs, illuminated and non-illuminated with focus on Neon sign.

voyage.name: Deutsche Oper Berlin
voyage.content: Classic opera house of West Berlin.

voyage.name: Schaubühne am Lehniner Platz
voyage.content: Modern theatre.

voyage.name: Theater am Kurfürstendamm
voyage.content: Popular theatre with TV celebrities in modern plays.

voyage.name: Schiller Theater
voyage.content: Used by the Komische Oper and temporarily as venue for the Komödie am Kurfürstendamm (im Schiller Theater). Between 2010 and 2018 it was used as temporary venue for Staatsoper Unter den Linden.

voyage.name: Theater des Westens
voyage.content: A historic theatre in the former West Berlin, only musicals today.

voyage.name: Grips Theater
voyage.content: Famous children's theatre with a light political touch, European recognition for the musical Linie 1.

voyage.name: Kant Kino
voyage.content: One of the few old cinemas (founded 1912) left in Berlin's western city. Mostly non-mainstream European movies.

voyage.name: Schlossgarten Charlottenburg
voyage.content: The green areas of the park are free, so you can go there to have a walk even if you are not interested in the palace. It covers a large area and you can get in from the entrance just near the "New Pavillon" (Neuer Pavillon a.k.a. Schinkelpavillon) placed on the right of Luisenplatz.

voyage.name: Lietzensee-Park
voyage.content: Lie in the grass and unwind at Lake Lietzensee, especially if you are with children - most of Charlottenburg children know and love the playground there.

voyage.name: Natur-Park Südgelände
voyage.content: The park is in an abandoned rail yard largely reclaimed by nature with trees and greenery growing around and within the tracks. Some tracks have been made over as footpaths for park visitors. The park has a retired steam locomotive on display as well as a few railway artifacts such as a turntable.

voyage.name: Spreefahrt
voyage.content: Do a boat tour on the Spree River or the Landwehrkanal - many of them start or end at Charlottenburg.

voyage.name: Artemis
voyage.content: When the unpredictable weather in Berlin isn't favourable to explore the city's cultural gems, Artemis makes up for it with its wellness facilities. Aimed at relaxation, no children or electronic devices are allowed to make a full disconnection from real world worries possible. Amenities include indoor and outdoor (heated) swimming pools and saunas, whirlpools, cinemas, and so on. Lunch and dinner are included in the

voyage.name: Arminiusmarkthalle
voyage.content: A market hall offering a mix of stalls with fresh and ready to eat produce (butchers, bakeries, delicatessen, etc.), and cafes and bars.

voyage.name: Feinkost Dalmatino
voyage.content: Cool little Croatian store. Sells excellent Croatian wines and many foodstuffs, and they also sell high-quality home-made slivovitz (plum liquor) from a big demijohn.

voyage.name: KaDeWe
voyage.content: The largest department store on the European continent at Wittenbergplatz has it all. Be sure to check out the food department at the sixth floor, where you can find anything from a baked chicken to a champagne brand bar. On the weekends, this place can get quite crowded.

voyage.name: Öz-Gida
voyage.content: There are Turkish supermarkets all over town, but this one is particularly big and has great items. If you want to have a picnic lunch, consider buying some small containers from their spreads counter, as they are really delicious! Good produce, too.

voyage.name: Philatelic Post Office
voyage.content: For collectible stamps. They generally speak English. From the Deutsche Post.

voyage.name: Café Sur
voyage.content: Deli that serves a delicious Mediterranean breakfast.

voyage.name: Cafe Bilderbuch
voyage.content: Café that is stocked with hundreds of books to rest and relax. Good cakes and sometimes on Sunday "Tanztee" (nipping tea and dancing) occurs.

voyage.name: Miss Honeypenny
voyage.content: Offers good à la carte breakfast

voyage.name: Potemkin
voyage.content: Russian restaurant that offers good breakfast varieties and a Sunday buffet. Also a popular coffee/cake break

voyage.name: Montevideo
voyage.content: Offers breakfast sets from around the world and also good lunch offers that attract the local residents

voyage.name: Charlottchen
voyage.content: Buffet breakfast and institution for parents and prepared for children of all ages, indoor play room!

voyage.name: Grüne Lampe
voyage.content: Excellent Russian breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: Café im Literaturhaus
voyage.content: Classical style, waiters in livrée.

voyage.name: Curry Wolf Kurfürstendamm
voyage.content: at Breitscheidplatz with Kaiser-Wilhelm-Memorial-Church.

voyage.name: RISA Chicken
voyage.content: The Berlin version of Kentucky Fried Chicken

voyage.name: Ratzfatzsatt
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Risa Chicken
voyage.content: The Berlin version of Kentucky Fried Chicken

voyage.name: Thomas-Eck Berlin
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Caffè e Gelato
voyage.content: Consistently great ice cream, ice cream-based desserts and the like. There are interesting flavours such as yogurt with figs and attacke, which includes chocolate and coconut, but the flavours don't vary from day to day, and there isn't a single flavour that is of inferior quality or taste. They have a larger branch at Postdamer Platz.

voyage.name: Raststätte Gnadenbrot
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Ratskeller Schöneberg
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Pinelli
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Genazvale
voyage.price: appetizers: €4-23, salads: €12-22, breads: €12-23; dumplings: €3-4; soups: €9-11; vegetables: €9-18; mains: €17-27
voyage.content: Delicious Georgian restaurant with pretty decor including Georgian rugs, some of them depicting ancient Georgian churches, and old photographs of people in traditional Georgian garb, and a sound track of pleasant Georgian music.

voyage.name: Vapiano
voyage.content: International chain with Italian food (pizza, pasta & salads) with an interesting approach of self-service. They prepare the meal in front of your eyes. The menu is also available in English and the entire staff speaks English.

voyage.name: Schweighofer's
voyage.content: Excellent Austrian restaurant with a great atmosphere. It is decorated as Austrian living rooms. Very generous portions, but you are welcome to share a course between more people as a starter or desserts. Try the brettljause or tafelspitz, which come highly recommended.

voyage.name: Lusiada
voyage.content: Portuguese restaurant famous for its mussels.

voyage.name: Good Friends
voyage.content: Original Chinese food, which may differ from the European "Chinese taste".

voyage.name: Block House
voyage.content: A number of restaurants in Berlin, where you can taste wonderful steaks.

voyage.name: El Dorado
voyage.content: This restaurant is a great steak house, serving sublime Spanish cuisine. Seating is available outside.

voyage.name: Bellucci
voyage.content: Great pizzas and professional service. Not a family restaurant, but kids are welcome and well cared for.

voyage.name: Tiergartenquelle
voyage.content: Real German dishes, properly prepared and big. Also some local beers available.

voyage.name: Restaurant Angkor Wat
voyage.content: Very good Cambodian restaurant with authentic style. Lunch & dinner sets are excellent values.

voyage.name: Agni
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 11:00-15:00 and 18:00-22:00; Sat Sun and holidays 18:00-22:00
voyage.content: Excellent Indian food.

voyage.name: Atlantik Fischrestaurant
voyage.price: appetizers: €9.50-19.90, soups: €8.50-11.90, salad: €9.90-19.50, sides: €4.90-7.50, fish and seafood mains: €19.90-35.00, fish sandwiches: €11.00-12.50
voyage.content: This Turkish fish restaurant is literally in a fish store, so when you order your fish or seafood, they take it from the counter where it's been kept on ice and cook it, so it's extremely fresh. The mains are quite large, so a couple with a large appetite could easily be satisfied sharing a main and a salad or side. The fish sandwiches are also very big.

voyage.name: Prince of Punjab
voyage.content: Excellent Indian food.

voyage.name: Buddha house
voyage.content: Mixture of Nepalese and Thai food/ You can reserve traditional tables (sitting on cushions, not on chairs).

voyage.name: Gottlob
voyage.content: Italian inspired kitchen with excellent weekend buffet or à la carte breakfast.

voyage.name: Ixthys
voyage.content: A tiny authentic Korean restaurant.

voyage.name: Papaya
voyage.content: Good Thai restaurant with original dishes from Isaan and consistent to that interior

voyage.name: Schöneberger Weltlaterne
voyage.content: Very traditional Bavarian kitchen & beers

voyage.name: Shayan
voyage.content: This is a family run Iranian restaurant with excellent Persian cuisine. Marinated lamb kebabs and the vegetarian khoreshteh esphinaj (stew) are recommended. Don't forget to order the delicious tea at the end of your meal!

voyage.name: Taverna Ousies
voyage.content: One of the best Greek restaurants along town. Always wise to make a reservation, sometimes a bit noisy.

voyage.name: Wiesenstein
voyage.content: Excellent Schwäbisches Food with good Schwaben wines in nice surrounding and neat garden

voyage.name: Ypsilon
voyage.content: Serving tasty Greek dishes with a good wine selection to match. Has a big biergarten for the balmy summer nights and plays live Greek music on Friday and Saturday.

voyage.name: Mar y Sol
voyage.content: Tapas and Spanish food

voyage.name: Eiffel
voyage.content: Good French restaurant with good value business lunch sets and interesting dinner variations.

voyage.name: 12 Apostel
voyage.content: Excellent Italian food and one of the best pizzas in town, Bleibtreustr. 49 (opposite S-Bahnstation Savignyplatz), 10623 Berlin (in Charlottenburg, and Hohenzollerndamm 33 in Wilmersdorf. Branches in Steglitz and Mitte.

voyage.name: Kuchi
voyage.content: One of the best sushi restaurants in Berlin. Also serves good pan Asian dishes.

voyage.name: Moustache
voyage.content: Excellent cuisine franchise next to the river, for the expatriate French in Berlin.

voyage.name: Sankt Moritz
voyage.content: Member of "Chaine des Rotisseurs" with outstanding wine card and excellent cuisine in rooms made by German painter. Named "Maitre of the year 2008".

voyage.name: Daitokai
voyage.content: The best teppanyaki grill in town.

voyage.name: Brauhaus Lemke am Schloß
voyage.content: Excellent brewed beer. You can have either a helles (light) or a dunkles (dark). Although the beer is quite excellent, the atmosphere is quite touristy, and clearly not as antique as it strives to be.

voyage.name: Coma
voyage.content: Made up with sand on the floor and two pool tables. XL Cocktails will kick you faster than you would think.

voyage.name: Green Door
voyage.content: One of the best cocktail bars in Berlin with excellent selection of spirits and a stylish decor to match.

voyage.name: Green Mango
voyage.content: The biggest karaokebar in Europe and they also have 150.000 karaoke playback.

voyage.name: Leydicke
voyage.content: One of the famous Berlin watering holes with a wide range of fruit wines, being drunk in nearly unchanged setting for the last 100 years. If the party gets started, among the best places in Berlin. Dangerous, when you come back to the fresh air.

voyage.name: Salut!
voyage.content: Cafe/bar that offers an impressive cocktail list. Cocktails are mixed with fresh juices and matched with quality spirits.

voyage.name: Train
voyage.content: As its name suggests, this bar is actually in an old S-Bahn car. Flashy and famous for inspired cocktails served by friendly bartenders.

voyage.name: Zur U-Bahn
voyage.content: One of the last old time Berlin bars in the area, and a great place to sit, drink and meet the locals.

voyage.name: Gitan Wein und Feinkost
voyage.content: Small wine bar with seats on footpath and some inside. Charming tree lined street. The proprietor and the shop look to be at least 500 years old perhaps more. Good selection of wine and charcuterie inside. This is not the spot for drinking and dancing until dawn but it can't be beaten if you are looking for a couple of quiet drinks in the afternoon.

voyage.name: Zig Zag Jazz Club
voyage.content: Very small cafe/bar with plenty of seating. Musicians play their original compositions most nights of the week. Quality is very high. Small snacks served but probably best to eat before you go as there is not much room.You can normally get tickets on the night if you are there at 8PM sharp but probably safest to book.

voyage.name: Cascade
voyage.content: similar to the Maxxim, but less r'n'b music, for the wealthy people of Charlottenburg. Nice interior, plays house and 70s/80s.

voyage.name: Havanna
voyage.content: Largest Latin music club in town. Dance to the beat when it's open on Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday nights.

voyage.name: Heideglühen
voyage.content: Sheltered open-air location at the waterside right across from the Westhafen harbor with techno, house, electro DJs.

voyage.name: Maxxim
voyage.content: A bit more luxurious for the more mature crowd. Mainly R'n'B and house.

voyage.name: Q-dorf
voyage.content: Named after the Ku'Damm, this big disco attracts a very young (and drunken) crowd. Rather cheap and usually very crowded with all the stuff you need (or don't want): R'n'B straight from the charts, Eurotrash party music, Mallorca ambiance, beach parties, go-go dancers and so on.

voyage.name: Amstel House Berlin
voyage.price: Four-bedded dorms from €12/person/night. Single and twin rooms en-suite also available
voyage.content: A newly refurbished guest house in an Art Nouveau style building.

voyage.name: Gasteiner Hof
voyage.content: The staff is friendly and helpful, and the breakfast is good. Some rooms have shared bathrooms, which can be quite cold at night.

voyage.name: Jet Pak City
voyage.price: Double rooms start at €30 per person, sleeping hall starts at €18 per person
voyage.content: Award-winning popular hostel.

voyage.name: Meininger Hotel Berlin Central Station
voyage.price: Double Rooms start at €39 per person, dormitory starts at €21

voyage.name: TRYP Berlin am Ku'damm
voyage.alt: formerly Grand City Hotel, hotel Imperial
voyage.content: One of the hotels in Lietzenburger Straße, parallel to the Ku'damm.

voyage.name: Hotel Pension Rotdorn
voyage.content: Ideal for visitors of the fairground. Small and reasonably priced hotel with large garden and wonderful ambiance.

voyage.name: Hotel Pension Am Park
voyage.content: Fairground in walking distance. Small house, personal, individual atmosphere.

voyage.name: Hotel Pension Bismarck
voyage.content: Small, familiar run house with personal ambiance.

voyage.name: Hotel Domicil
voyage.content: Private hotel.

voyage.name: Hotel Alexander
voyage.content: Very clean and friendly hotel in a nice neighborhood.

voyage.name: Ku'Damm 101
voyage.content: Three-star hotel for business travellers with a sense of lifestyle and design. Wi-fi available for a small fee (€1.90 per hour, €3 for two hours, etc.) or free internet from two terminals in the lobby.

voyage.name: Swissotel
voyage.content: Brand new and stylish design hotel direct at the Ku'Damm. Just a step away from anything in the City West and offers good weekend rates. One of the best hotel restaurants in town.

voyage.name: Steigenberger
voyage.content: Los-Angeles-Platz 1. Located at a quiet square near Kurfürstendamm.

voyage.name: Q!hotel
voyage.content: This hotel makes the most of its small spaces by wrapping them in striking design based on white, black and dark red, as well as geometric curves and concaves. Some rooms have unusual features, such as bathtubs right next to the beds. The name of the hotel is a play on the Ku'damm, ("Q" = "Ku"), as well as the German word for cow ("Kuh", pronounced the same as "Q" or "Ku").

voyage.name: Louisa’s Place
voyage.content: Small but luxurious boutique hotel with charm in a historic city villa.

voyage.name: Dormero Hotel Berlin Ku'damm
voyage.content: Located in a quiet corner of City West, this cozy hotel features a very good restaurant.

voyage.name: Schlosshotel im Grunewald
voyage.content: Tucked away near the Grunewald Castle, this ultra luxe exudes charm and indulgence, and with the interior styled by Karl Lagerfield, you can be assured of a stylish setting. May be the luxury hotel with the greenest surroundings in Berlin, a step away from the hectic part of the city. Was home to the German national soccer team during the World Cup 2006.

voyage.name: Wyndham Berlin Excelsior Hotel
voyage.content: The ageing Hotel Excelsior became a Wyndham and was afforded a renovation of its common areas and the deluxe rooms. Others remain tired, however, and not always meet guest's expectations. The limited Internet access also does not help the hotel score highly. The hotel faces the green wide Hardenbergstraße, northwest of the Zoologischer Garten train station, its courtyard side is also overlooking a nice, green area.

voyage.name: Waldorf Astoria
voyage.content: The Berlin property of Hilton's uber-luxury chain has some of the best views in Berlin, being located at the upper floors of the Zoofenster tower. The location is also first rate, right between the Gedachniskirche and the Zoologischer Garten train station. That said, the prices are among the highest in Berlin as well.

voyage.name: Sofitel Berlin Kurfurstendamm
voyage.content: The distinctive, multi-tiered wedding cake of a hotel peeks out from behind the Swissotel at the corner of Augsburger and Joachimstaler Straßen, making one of the few remarkable architectural statements along the Kurfurstendamm. It was launched as the Concorde Berlin, and became a Sofitel at the start of 2014, retaining pretty much everything but the name - including the simple yet refined decor throughout the hotel

voyage.name: Checkpoint Charlie
voyage.content: It was the only border crossing between East and West Berlin that permitted foreigners passage. Residents of East and West Berlin were not allowed to use it. This contributed to Checkpoint Charlie's mythological status as a meeting place for spies and other shady individuals. Checkpoint Charlie gained its name from the phonetic alphabet; checkpoints "Alpha" and "Bravo" were at the autobahn checkpoints Helmstedt and D

voyage.name: Oranienstraße
voyage.content: A street full of shops, cafes and restaurants

voyage.name: Bergmannstraße
voyage.content: Like Oranienstraße a street full of shops, cafes and restaurants, but in the other, more middle-class part of Kreuzberg.

voyage.name: Görlitzer Park
voyage.content: 150-200 m along the Wiener Straße (bypassing the fire house and the public swimming pool) from U-Bahn Görlitzer Bahnhof, the park is famous for the Turkish families barbecuing on summer weekends, failed contemporary art and relaxed atmosphere of students. It does have a reputation of being full of pickpockets and drug dealers though and the police makes regular visits to this place to check on the situation.

voyage.name: Landwehrkanal
voyage.content: Take a stroll for a few kilometers along this canal which runs right through the heart of Kreuzberg. It's peaceful and mostly traffic-free, but full of life in summer. Some parts are lined with bars and restaurants with terraces. Sit on a bench or terrace and watch the world go by on a summer evening.

voyage.name: Viktoriapark
voyage.content: With the Kreuzberg, a hill in Kreuzberg 61, the Prussian National Monument by Schinkel and a waterfall. Superb panoramic views across south Berlin.

voyage.name: Meistersaal
voyage.content: Though the area has changed a lot, the building with the Meistersaal, an old music hall from the 1900s, has persisted. Later converted into sound studios, music history was written here with David Bowie ("Heroes"), Iggy Pop, and U2 amongst the groups who recorded here at the "Studio by the wall". Guided tours available occasionally.

voyage.name: Topography of Terror
voyage.content: This outdoor and indoor history museum documents the terror applied by the Nazi regime. It is on the site of buildings which during the Nazi regime from 1933 to 1945 were the headquarters of the Gestapo and the SS, the principal instruments of repression during the Nazi era.

voyage.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
voyage.price: Adults €6, concessions €3. Reduced admission if you show a ticket from the nearby Berlinische Galerie
voyage.content: Designed by Daniel Libeskind with an excellent exposition on the Jewish life in Berlin and the impact of the Holocaust. You can easily spend a day here. There is a metal scanner and other security features you'd rather expect at an airport than a museum.

voyage.name: Martin-Gropius-Bau
voyage.price: Around €10, varies between exhibits. Free for ages 16 and under
voyage.content: It was a museum of applied arts and a listed historical monument since 1966, and it is now a well-known Berlin exhibition hall.

voyage.name: Berlinische Galerie
voyage.price: Adults 8 EUR, concessions 5 EUR, under 18 free. Every first Monday of the month €4. Reduced admission if you show a ticket from the nearby Jewish Museum
voyage.content: A museum of modern art, photography and architecture. Its collection focuses on art created in Berlin.

voyage.name: German Museum of Technology
voyage.content: Huge technical museum, on a former railroad depot, featuring from ancient water and wind mills to computer pioneer Konrad Zuse's inventions, a collection of old to new vehicles of all types -bicycles, boats, trains, etc - and the interactive Spectrum science center with various hands-on experiments. There's an actual C-17 "Candy Bomber" airplane hanging on its façade. The railroad and aeronautical sections are hard t

voyage.name: East Side Gallery
voyage.content: The longest stretch of the Berlin Wall still in existence, painted by artists in 1991 and restored in 2009, after years of decay. At Mühlenstraße, next to the river Spree. The murals are painted on the east side of the wall after the fall of Communism; so they are not from the Cold War, during which murals could only be painted on the west side. Make sure not to miss the famous mural of a car seemingly crashing throu

voyage.name: Simon-Dach-Straße
voyage.content: The heart of Friedrichshain and its nightlife with numerous cafés, bars and restaurants along its entire extent and also in the side streets.

voyage.name: Boxhagener Platz and surroundings
voyage.content: The area around Boxhagener Platz is filled with bars, cafes and small shops. Boxhagener Platz itself is a small park with a playground and a cafe, and the nearby Simon Dach Straße is filled with cheap bars and restaurants. At the weekend you can find many places that serve the famous, cheap Berliner brunch. On Sundays there is a small flea market worth strolling around

voyage.name: Computerspielemuseum
voyage.content: Exhibition of digital interactive entertainment culture. You can actually play almost all of the exhibits making it a more "hands on" museum than most.

voyage.name: Oberbaum Bridge
voyage.content: Arguably the most beautiful bridge in Berlin and the only connection between Friedrichshain and Kreuzberg. As signage on the bridge indicates, it was built twice - once in the 1890s and once in the 1990s. Before reunification the border ran where the bridge now is.

voyage.name: Karl-Marx-Allee
voyage.content: The main street of former East Berlin. It is a big avenue, featuring neoclassical East German buildings, fountains and lakes.

voyage.name: Märchenbrunnen
voyage.content: In 1893 the authorities of Berlin issued the artistic entrance to the National Park Friedrichshain. The fountain of fairy tales was commissioned by the National Park and later designed by Ludwig Hoffmann.
